slides.0.title: Grape varieties
slides.0.subtitle: A "vine museum"
slides.1.title: Two worlds
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Bordeaux-style varieties
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Near Bordeaux, Bergerac and Côtes de Duras use Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Sauvignon and Sémillon (Wikipedia, VinePair)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Native varieties
slides.1.highlights.1.content: wein.plus calls it a "vine museum": Tannat, Négrette, Mauzac, Manseng Noir, Arrufiac, Baroque, Duras, Fer, Lauzet, Len de l'El and more
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Many names for one grape
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Malbec is Côt, Auxerrois or Pressac in Cahors; Fer Servadou is Braucol in Gaillac, Mansois in Marcillac and Pinenc in Madiran
slides.1.content: The further south and closer to the Pyrenees, the more native varieties appear.
slides.2.title: Black Malbec and Tannat
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Malbec (Côt)
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Cahors requires at least 70% Malbec, with Merlot and Tannat each allowed up to 30% (Wine With Seth); flavours include plum and tobacco (Wine Folly)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Tannat
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Its name comes from the Langue d'Oc "tan", to tan; thick skins rich in anthocyanins give almost black, very astringent wines with high body, acidity and tannin (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Uruguay
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The Basque immigrant Harriague brought Tannat to Uruguay in 1870, and by INAVI's 2018 figures it covered 1,610 ha, the most planted variety (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.content: Malbec leans fruity and supple, while Tannat is about power and tannin.
slides.3.title: Other native reds
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Négrette
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Low acidity and tannin but deep colour; violet, raspberry and licorice; best on boulbènes soils; sold in California as Pinot St-George until 1997 (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Fer Servadou
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Its name comes from the French word for iron, for the vine's very hard wood; Marcillac wines can be tannic and rustic, elsewhere it gives redcurrant and rhubarb notes (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Gaillac red rules
slides.3.highlights.2.content: At least two of Duras, Braucol (Fer), Prunelart and Syrah, together at least 70% (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.content: These varieties are rare elsewhere and give the South-West its identity.
slides.4.title: White grapes
slides.4.highlights.0.title: The Manseng family
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Gros Manseng is a natural offspring of Petit Manseng (DNA analysis), which is itself a progeny of Savagnin; France has about 2,800 ha of Gros and about 600 ha of Petit (Wine With Seth)
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Mauzac
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Native to the South-West, mainly in Gaillac and Limoux; late budding and ripening; about 3,200 ha in France in 2000 (Wikipedia)
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Supporting varieties
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Jurançon's supporting varieties are Courbu Blanc, Petit Courbu, Camaralet de Lasseube and Lauzet (Wine With Seth); Gaillac whites use Len de l'El, Mauzac and Muscadelle
slides.4.content: Among whites, high-acid, aromatic Manseng and sparkling-capable Mauzac lead the way.
